candidates.name: cdx_toolkit
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Common Crawl org's Python toolkit for querying CDX indices (Common Crawl and Internet Archive Wayback). Pulls index rows and fetches WARC records by offset/length; no committed dataset, purely a client library/CLI. 211 stars, Apache-2.0, updated 7 Sep 2026 (actively maintained).
candidates.why_useful: This is almost certainly the tool underlying our existing Common Crawl CDX index over airbnb.com (2.08M rows, 50 crawls) and the 3,000 WARC renders we already hold; documents how to re-pull or extend that index to more crawls, other domains (Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia, competitor STR platforms), or historical date ranges for the same host — directly extends gap targets 9 (competitor supply) and 17 (methods).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: We already hold a CC CDX index over airbnb.com and WARC renders; this is the generating tool, not new data

candidates.name: warcio
candidates.what_it_holds: Streaming WARC/ARC record reader/writer library (Python), used to parse the WARC files that cdx_toolkit or direct CC fetches return. 472 stars, Apache-2.0, updated 8 Sep 2026, actively maintained by the Webrecorder/Internet Archive-adjacent team.
candidates.why_useful: Needed to actually read the 3,000 WARC renders we already captured, or any new WARC pulls for competitor sites (Vrbo, Sonder, Vacasa, Hipcamp listing pages) to extract page text/prices/counts at a point in time.

candidates.name: warcio.js
candidates.what_it_holds: JavaScript/Node port of warcio for streaming WARC IO in browser or Node contexts. 55 stars, MIT, updated 4 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Alternative WARC-reading tool if any pipeline work moves to a JS/browser context (e.g. a Wayback-viewer style tool for archived AirDNA or STR-platform pages).

candidates.name: scrapy-warcio
candidates.what_it_holds: Internet Archive extension adding WARC-writing support to the Scrapy crawling framework. 24 stars, updated 15 Dec 2025.
candidates.why_useful: Would let a future (human-approved) scrape of a non-Airbnb STR/travel site be captured in standard WARC format so it becomes point-in-time archivable, consistent with how Common Crawl stores pages.

candidates.name: warc-stat
candidates.what_it_holds: Small CLI that summarizes a WARC file's contents as JSON: record types, hosts, HTTP status codes, MIME types, failed captures. 0 stars, updated 30 Jul 2026, no committed data.
candidates.why_useful: Quick QA/inventory tool for auditing our existing 3,000 WARC renders (coverage by host/status code) before deeper parsing work.

candidates.name: 72m-domains-dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: 72,475,235 unique registered domains extracted via DuckDB from Common Crawl's cc-index columnar Parquet files, deduplicated across 14 monthly snapshots Jan 2025-Feb 2026. Stored as Parquet (built from an SQLite intermediate). 25 stars, license 'Other', updated 1 Sep 2026, actively maintained.
candidates.why_useful: A monthly-cadence global domain-presence list built directly from the cc-index columnar query pattern named in this theme; could be used to check month-by-month whether specific competitor/STR-adjacent domains (Vrbo, Hipcamp, Sonder, Tujia, Xiaozhu, AllTheRooms) are crawled/indexed at all, and shows exactly how to run the same cc-index Parquet query ourselves for a custom domain list or date range.

candidates.name: common-crawl-ranks-cache
candidates.what_it_holds: Daily-polled (effectively quarterly, since CC webgraph releases are quarterly) mirror of Common Crawl's host- and domain-level web-graph ranks, Top-1M per release. Host-level CSV: rank, harmonic-centrality score, PageRank position, PageRank value, hostname. Domain-level CSV adds distinct-host count per domain. Gzip-compressed CSVs in a GitHub Actions-driven repo; no stated start date/backfill (tracks only from first cron run), license 'Other'.
candidates.why_useful: Directly answers gap 5 (web-traffic/engagement proxies: Tranco/Common Crawl host-graph ranks). If airbnb.com (and Vrbo, Booking.com, Expedia domains) sit inside the Top-1M, this gives a free, repeatable time series of relative web-graph prominence per CC quarterly release that could proxy for site engagement/traffic momentum, complementing the missing Similarweb/Cloudflare Radar data.
candidates.time_coverage: from first cron run (recent) forward, refreshed ~quarterly with CC webgraph releases
candidates.size_hint: Top-1M hosts/domains per release, gzip CSV

candidates.name: get-common-crawl
candidates.what_it_holds: Small French-language script that downloads the Common Crawl web-graph archive and produces a 3-column file (PageRank rank, domain, subdomain count). 0 stars, no license, last updated 2 Mar 2023.
candidates.why_useful: A simpler/older alternative method to build the same kind of host-rank series as common-crawl-ranks-cache, useful as a fallback if that repo's cache format changes.

candidates.name: arrhivescrape
candidates.what_it_holds: Reusable Wayback Machine / CDX-based static-site recovery toolkit with a CLI and local web UI, for reconstructing archived versions of a site from CDX index entries. 0 stars, no license, updated 26 Jun 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Matches gap 17's 'Wayback Machine tooling (archived airbnb.com pages, archived AirDNA market pages)' — could be pointed (with human sign-off, not run by an agent) at archived AirDNA market pages or historical airbnb.com pages already indexed by CDX to reconstruct point-in-time snapshots.

candidates.name: time-travelling-web-search-monster
candidates.what_it_holds: Old (last updated 2019) Clojure tool to search for phrases across Common Crawl's web archive. 1 star, Apache-2.0.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: a phrase-search-over-CC-archive method that could in principle scan historical crawls for mentions of STR platforms/regulation terms, but stale and unmaintained.

candidates.name: cdxlab
candidates.what_it_holds: Stated as 'Training for the CDX toolkit' — 0 stars, no license, last updated 2021. Likely a tutorial/practice repo rather than a working pipeline.
candidates.why_useful: Very low value; flagged only for completeness since it surfaced under the cdx-toolkit search term.

notes: Hard-capped at 6 `gh search repos` calls per instructions; all 6 used (cdx-toolkit, "common crawl" travel, warcio, "common crawl" hotel, "common crawl" rank domain, cc-index columnar). Direct 'common crawl'+travel and 'common crawl'+hotel searches returned almost nothing (1 irrelevant hit, 0 hits) — there is no popular GitHub repo that has already extracted a travel/hotel-specific dataset FROM Common Crawl; the useful hits are all general-purpose CC tooling (cdx_toolkit, warcio family) or general host/domain-rank mirrors (wangmm001/common-crawl-ranks-cache, digitalcortex/72m-domains-dataset) that WOULD have to be pointed at travel domains by us. Two WebFetch README pulls succeeded (ranks-cache, 72m-domains); a third (cdx_toolkit README.rst) 404'd — wrong filename guess, not worth a retry given budget. Both WebSearch calls failed because this session's WebSearch budget (200/session, shared conversation-wide) was already exhausted before this scout ran, so I could not do the site:github.com fallback search for 'common crawl airbnb' or 'common crawl booking.com/expedia/vrbo' terms the task suggested as a fallback; a future scout with WebSearch budget remaining should try those two queries plus 'common crawl' 'short-term rental' and 'cc-index' vrbo/hipcamp. Best single find for our numbered gaps is wangmm001/common-crawl-ranks-cache against gap 5 (web-traffic/engagement rank proxy) — worth a human check of whether airbnb.com/competitor domains actually appear in its Top-1M files before investing more time. No repo found that mirrors historical (pre-2023) Inside Airbnb dumps via Common Crawl, and no repo found scraping/deriving data specifically from Vrbo, Sonder, Vacasa, Hipcamp, or Chinese STR platforms via CC tooling — that remains an open gap for another scout/modality (e.g. a direct cdx_toolkit query against those hostnames, not a GitHub search).
